title: Sensex Jumps 1,109 Points as IT Rally and Rupee Recovery Drive Best Session in Four Months
excerpt: The Sensex closed at 73,033.78 and the Nifty at 22,721.95 on Tuesday. HCLTech surged 8.28% on a 21% profit rise, TCS gained 6.59%, the Nifty IT index jumped over 5%, and breadth stayed weak beneath the headline — declines outnumbered advances on the BSE.
body:
• The BSE Sensex jumped 1,109.10 points, or 1.54%, to close at 73,033.78 — its best single-day gain in four months; the NSE Nifty rose 358.60 points, or 1.60%, to 22,721.95.
  • HCLTech led the rally, surging 8.28% after reporting a 21.18% rise in consolidated net profit to ₹5,132 crore for the July–September quarter; TCS rose 6.59%, Tech Mahindra 4.90% and Infosys 4.44%.
  • The rally added more than ₹3.89 lakh crore to the market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies, taking total market wealth to around ₹469 lakh crore.
  • The advance was narrow: on the BSE, 2,335 stocks fell against 1,806 gainers, and analysts flagged crude at about $104.55 a barrel and September retail inflation of 5.54% as headwinds.

Indian equities staged their sharpest rebound in months on Tuesday, powered by technology earnings, a recovering rupee and a Finance Minister comment that traders chose to read as an opening on capital-gains taxes. The 30-share BSE Sensex jumped 1,109.10 points, or 1.54 per cent, to settle near the day's high at 73,033.78, posting its best single-day gain in four months, PTI reported. The NSE Nifty climbed 358.60 points, or 1.60 per cent, to 22,721.95 — its best single-day rebound in more than two months.

IT did the heavy lifting

The session belonged to the technology sector after HCLTech reported a 21.18 per cent rise in consolidated net profit to ₹5,132 crore for the July–September quarter of FY27, helped by higher margins from its fast-growing advanced AI operations and a lower tax outgo; its AI business annualised revenue rose to $219 million from $171 million in the preceding quarter. HCLTech stock surged 8.28 per cent, TCS gained 6.59 per cent, Tech Mahindra 4.90 per cent and Infosys 4.44 per cent, taking the Nifty IT index up more than 5 per cent. Financials and defensives joined in — HUL, Titan, Bajaj Finserv, SBI, HDFC Bank, M&M and ICICI Bank were among the major movers — while Kotak Mahindra Bank, Eternal and Maruti Suzuki lagged.

"Indian equities advanced as stronger-than-expected technology earnings boosted confidence in corporate profit growth and lifted benchmark-heavy large-cap stocks. Rupee stability and easing bond yields further supported sentiment, bringing financial stocks into focus."

— Vinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments

The caveats under the headline

Two supports came from outside the earnings calendar. The rupee extended its recovery after the RBI's weekend measures to curb volatility — a stabilisation Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman endorsed publicly on Tuesday — and Brent crude eased 1.66 per cent to $104.6 a barrel. She also described the debate on long-term capital gains tax and STT rationalisation as "healthy," remarks the market treated as a signal ahead of the February Budget.

Breadth, however, told a more cautious story. Declines outnumbered advances on the BSE — 2,335 stocks fell against 1,806 gainers — stocks at 52-week lows outnumbered those at 52-week highs, and the India VIX's 8 per cent fall sat alongside weakness in small-caps. With September retail inflation at 5.54 per cent and crude still above $104, Tuesday's rally is best read as an earnings-led large-cap rebound, not yet a broad change in market weather. The next test is whether the IT results season — with more majors reporting this week — confirms HCLTech's numbers as a sector trend.
